title: Giouvarlakia
subtitle: Greek meatballs in a lemon and egg broth
excerpt: Soft lamb and rice meatballs simmered in broth and finished with a silky avgolemono sauce of egg and lemon. A Greek soup-stew that is warming and sharp in equal measure.
sourceNotes: Traditional Greek soup, closely related to the broader avgolemono family. Synthesised from multiple Greek home cook sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Form the meatballs up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Add them to the broth just before serving. Do not make the avgolemono ahead.

content.text: Giouvarlakia is a Greek meatball soup finished with avgolemono. The egg and lemon sauce must be tempered slowly or it will scramble. Keep the broth below a simmer when you stir it in.
Combine the mince, raw rice, grated onion, parsley, dried mint, beaten egg, salt and pepper in a bowl. Mix well with your hands. Shape into walnut-sized balls.
Bring the stock to a steady simmer in a large pan. Add the olive oil.
Lower the meatballs in gently one by one. Do not stir for the first 5 minutes or they will break apart.
Simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through and the rice is tender.
Make the avgolemono. Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks in a bowl. Beat in the yolks. Whisk in the lemon juice.
Ladle about 3 ladlefuls of hot broth into the egg mixture very slowly, whisking constantly. This tempers the eggs.
Remove the pan from the heat. Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the soup slowly while stirring. Do not return to the boil. Serve straight away.

items.cause: The hot broth was added to the eggs too fast, or the soup was still on the boil when the sauce went in.
items.fix: Add the broth to the eggs one ladleful at a time, whisking after each. Always take the pot off the heat before adding the sauce.

items.cause: They were stirred too soon, or the mix was too loose.
items.fix: Leave them untouched for the first 5 minutes after lowering in. Add an extra tablespoon of raw rice to the mix if it feels wet.

items.symptom: The soup is thin and flat.
items.cause: The stock was weak, or not enough lemon was used.
items.fix: Start with a good flavoured stock. The avgolemono should be assertively lemony; taste and add more juice if needed.
